# ACME 2026 Proposal

This fabricated proposal was authored on 2026-02-03 by agent:bob-engineer. The label ACME is used only as a generic fictional account name for a fixture and does not refer to a real client.

The proposal recommends a small markdown-first knowledge workflow. Incoming notes would be classified by type, key actors would use CURIE identifiers, and decision records would carry explicit supersedence fields. The proposal also asks reviewers to keep evidence links separate from commitments so overdue promises remain visible until closed.

The document is a Q2 golden query target. A test that asks for a proposal authored by `agent:bob-engineer` on 2026-02-03 should match this file, especially if it filters by `type: proposal`, `authored_at`, or the author identifier in frontmatter.

## Proposed Scope

The proposed scope includes a one-week vault audit, a two-week cleanup pass, and a final review meeting. The work is intentionally small so the fixture does not imply a complete delivery program.

The synthetic review team would inspect stale commitments, authority aliases, and decision chains. Findings would be recorded as markdown notes with clear timestamps and stable identifiers. No actual procurement, billing, domain, or named customer workflow is represented.

## Review Criteria

The proposal should be considered ready for test retrieval when the parser can read the author, date, proposal identifier, and draft status. The body gives additional natural-language hints, but the frontmatter is the canonical structured source for the fixture.

## Delivery Approach

The proposed delivery uses a deliberately small pass over a synthetic vault. The first pass checks only file shape and required metadata. The second pass checks relationships between commitments, decisions, transcripts, and authority records. The final pass writes a short review note that explains any unresolved drift.

This staged approach keeps the fixture useful for search tests and graph tests without adding a fake implementation plan. It also makes the authored date and author field easy to validate in isolation from the rest of the vault.
